steps.stem: Pnina instructed the staff of her clothes shop to play up-to-date music in the shop, in the hope that it would raise sales. After a few weeks she found that sales had fallen, and she attributed the fall to the music. Which of the following facts would support Pnina's explanation?
choices: The clothes in her shop are designed along unusual lines, unlike what is common in the market
The supermarket next to her shop plays up-to-date music and is always full of customers
In Pnina's other shops, where no up-to-date music was played, sales did not change over the same period
A week before Pnina gave her instruction, a new shop opened nearby, offering good clothes at low prices
explanation: Shops without the music saw no fall — the music is what differed. (4) supplies a rival cause; (2) and (1) cut the other way or not at all.

steps.stem: Mr. Cohen noticed that his neighbor Mr. Levi had thrown several household objects made of blue glass into the rubbish. He concluded that Mr. Levi does not like objects made of blue glass. Which of the following data does NOT weaken Mr. Cohen's conclusion?
choices: Mr. Levi received the blue glass objects a week before his birthday
All the objects in Mr. Levi's house are made of blue glass
The objects Mr. Levi threw away were cracked or broken
Mr. Levi's wife had recently bought a new set of household objects
explanation: When he received them has no bearing on why he discarded them; (2), (3) and (4) each offer a reason other than dislike.

steps.stem: In a study, Dr. Mor divided solvers of crossword puzzles into two groups — one of four members and one of ten — and asked each group to solve, working together, a crossword of the same kind. She found that the group of ten completed far more of the clues in the time allowed than the group of four, and she put forward the hypothesis that the size of a group influences its success at such tasks. Which of the following claims strengthens Dr. Mor's hypothesis?
choices: The members of the group of four were experienced solvers, whereas the members of the group of ten had rarely attempted a crossword before
Six of the members of the group of ten left the room before the group had begun to work on the crossword
One of the members of the group of ten had seen the crossword before the study and knew several of the answers in advance
The crossword given to the group of four was noticeably harder than the crossword given to the group of ten
explanation: If the larger group won despite being the less experienced, the size of the group is a stronger candidate for the cause. (3), (2) and (4) each supply a rival explanation of the result — prior knowledge, an effective group of four, an easier puzzle.

steps.stem: Given: the share of people suffering from high blood pressure among those who take the drug Cyclodin is higher than its share in the general population. Supposition: high blood pressure is a side effect of taking Cyclodin. Which of the following data would weaken the supposition?
choices: Cyclodin is a drug for headaches caused by high blood pressure
Those who take an alternative drug to Cyclodin do not suffer from high blood pressure
Physicians prescribe Cyclodin only to patients who do not suffer from high blood pressure
One of the main side effects of Cyclodin is stomach pain
explanation: If the drug is given to people who already have high blood pressure, the correlation runs the other way. (3) supports the supposition; (2) and (4) do not bear on it.

steps.stem: Ariel read in a newspaper article that dozens of studies have been published in scientific journals indicating a correlation between drinking large quantities of rose tea and improved health, and only two studies that did not find this correlation. He concluded that if he drinks large quantities of rose tea, his health will improve. Which of the following does not weaken his conclusion?
choices: Researchers tend to shelve studies that do not prove the correlation they wanted to find
Most of the studies that found a correlation between drinking the tea and improved health were funded by producers of rose tea, and this casts doubt on the credibility of the studies

The studies that did not find a correlation between drinking the tea and improved health were published in journals that are more reliable than the journals that published the studies that did find such a correlation
The studies that did not find a correlation between drinking the tea and improved health were conducted before the studies that did find such a correlation

steps.stem: In a certain school, pupils who commit disciplinary offenses such as arriving late for a lesson are sent to help the caretaker during the break. Last week the school introduced a new punishment for lateness — being sent to sit in the corridor outside the principal's office — and in the days that followed the number of latenesses recorded fell sharply. The school secretary concluded that the new punishment deters pupils. Which of the following facts would weaken the secretary's conclusion?
choices: At the beginning of last week the school announced that the class with the fewest disciplinary offenses this year would receive a prize
When the caretaker returned to work after a long absence, the number of latenesses recorded rose
Three weeks ago a record was set both in the number of latenesses recorded and in the number of pupils sent to help the caretaker
Last week daylight saving time began in the country, which makes it harder for pupils to get up on time in the morning
explanation: A prize announced at the same moment supplies another reason for the fall. (4) would have raised latenesses, so the fall despite it supports the secretary; (3) and (2) concern the old punishment.

steps.title: Strengthen and weaken — the toolkit
steps.intro: Every choice adds data. Ask which way it pushes the conclusion.

head: Weakens
Strengthens
rows: !Alternative explanation — another reason for the same data
!Negating an alternative explanation — the other reason is ruled out (or works against the result)
Counterexample — the cause without the effect
Supporting example — no cause, no effect
Chicken and egg — cause and effect swapped
Undermining the basis — the data behind the conclusion is shaky
Strengthening the basis — the data becomes even stronger

tips: Gambler test: bet on the conclusion — does the new fact shake your bet?
'Does NOT weaken': cross out the 3 that weaken — the answer may be irrelevant, not only strengthening.
Flip test: if the flipped fact weakens, the original strengthens.
Watch whether the data is a number or a percentage.
A clear-cut alternative explanation: mark it and move on.

steps.stem: In country A an experiment was conducted with infants between one and two years old, in which it was found that many of them recognize themselves in a mirror: the researchers painted a small mark on each infant's cheek without his noticing, and after a while set him before a mirror. Most of the infants reached for the mark on their own cheek, and did not try to wipe it from the mirror. When the researchers repeated the experiment in country B, however, most of the infants neither touched the mark nor tried to remove it. The researchers concluded that in country B the ability to recognize oneself develops later than in country A. Which of the following findings does NOT weaken the researchers' conclusion?
choices: In country A the proportion of infants who suffer from impaired vision is much higher than in country B
In country B it is customary to decorate infants' faces with painted marks, whereas in country A it is not
In another experiment, infants from country B succeeded in recognizing themselves in photographs, whereas infants from country A did not
Unlike infants in country A, infants in country B tend not to act without an explicit sign of permission
explanation: Poorer vision in A would make A's success harder to obtain, not easier — it leaves the conclusion intact or strengthens it. (3) shows the ability present in B; (2) and (4) explain B's behavior without any difference in recognition.

steps.stem: The director of a zoo wished to increase the number of camels in the zoo and brought a pair, male and female, from another zoo. After three months the female had still not become pregnant, and the director decided to move the pair to a much larger enclosure; shortly afterwards the female became pregnant. The director concluded that zoo animals need a large space in order to breed. Which of the following facts would weaken the director's conclusion?
choices: The last pair of camels brought to the zoo had not been moved to a larger enclosure
Camels require a long period of acquaintance before they mate
Camels are rarely seen in pairs in the wild
Before they were moved to the larger enclosure, the two camels had already known each other for a long time
explanation: If camels need time rather than space, the pregnancy after three months plus a move is explained by the time alone. (4) removes the time explanation and so supports the director; (1) and (3) do not bear on the cause.

steps.stem: The population of a certain country is made up of the members of two tribes, Alpha and Beta. A researcher found that only a few of the students at the royal academy are members of the Alpha tribe, and concluded that the academy's admission procedures discriminate against members of that tribe. Which of the following data would weaken the researcher's conclusion?
choices: The share of the Alpha tribe in the country's population is higher than its share among the students of the academy
The largest secondary school in the country is the school of the Alpha tribe
Most of the members of the academy's admissions committee are members of the Alpha tribe
The share of the Alpha tribe among all the students of the academy is higher than its share in the country's population
explanation: If Alpha's share at the academy exceeds its share in the population, its small number reflects a small tribe, not discrimination. (1) supports the researcher; (2) and (3) do not bear on the outcome.

steps.stem: Yifat read in a newspaper that in 1998 the number of tourists arriving in Syldavia did not rise in comparison with the previous year, although at the beginning of that year the Syldavian ministry of tourism had launched an advertising campaign in many countries. She judged that the reason is that Syldavia does not have enough hotel rooms. Which of the following facts would weaken Yifat's judgment?
choices: At the end of 1998 the procedures for obtaining a permit to build hotels in Syldavia were shortened
Because of the economic crisis in Syldavia in 1998, a holiday there became cheaper than it had been in 1997
The reactions around the world to the ministry's campaign were very favorable
In 1997 the hotels of Syldavia were not fully occupied even in a single month of the year
explanation: Empty rooms in the year before mean that room supply was not what held tourists back. (1) concerns the future; (2) and (3) make the flat figure more puzzling without touching the rooms.

steps.stem: Researchers examined two kinds of television advertisement to see which is the more effective: advertisements featuring unknown actors, and advertisements featuring celebrities from the entertainment industry. Their study found that the sales of a product promoted by a celebrity were higher than the sales of another product promoted by unknown actors, and they presented the main idea of their conclusion in the title of the article summarizing the study: "We Believe Only Those We Already Know." Which of the following statements could weaken the researchers' conclusion?
choices: An advertisement featuring a local celebrity is no less effective than an advertisement featuring a foreign celebrity
On the radio, unlike on television, most advertisers use celebrities from the entertainment industry
When unknown actors promote a product, the product too is perceived as unknown, and this makes consumers suspicious
Only companies whose products are already the most popular can afford to pay a celebrity to promote them
explanation: If the celebrity-promoted products were the popular ones to begin with, the sales gap has another cause. (3) offers a mechanism that supports the conclusion; (1) and (2) do not touch the comparison.

steps.stem: About a decade ago several insurance companies in the Netherlands began to require policy-holders living in ground-floor homes to install smart locks on their windows and doors. Recently the police reported that over the past decade the number of burglaries of ground-floor homes in the Netherlands fell by twenty percent, and police officials proposed a law requiring every homeowner to install smart locks, arguing that this would reduce burglaries throughout the country. Critics of the argument suggested that several investigations be carried out first. Which of the following investigations is NOT relevant to testing the police officials' argument?
choices: Over the past decade, did the proportion of ground-floor homes in the Netherlands fitted with alarm systems increase?
Over the past decade, did the number of homes on upper floors fitted with smart locks increase?
Does the fall in burglaries of ground-floor homes apply only to homes in which smart locks were installed?
Over the past decade, did the number of burglaries in the Netherlands as a whole fall, or only the number of burglaries of ground-floor homes?
explanation: Locks on upper floors have no bearing on why ground-floor burglaries fell. (1) tests a rival cause, (3) tests whether the locks are the cause, (4) tests whether the fall is general.

steps.stem: A study found that patients who took a medication for lowering blood fats at a fixed hour of the day had lower levels of blood fats than patients who did not take the medication at a fixed hour. In consequence the manufacturer issued guidelines that the medication should be taken at a fixed hour. A physician argued that the guideline was unjustified, basing his argument on a certain piece of information. Which of the following is most likely to be the information on which the physician relied?
choices: People who are careful about their health and lead a healthy way of life take their medication at a fixed hour
The medication given to the patients in the study had less effect than had been expected
Taking a medication at one particular hour is not necessarily more effective than taking it at another
Most people do not follow exactly the instructions in the patient leaflet
explanation: The people who keep a fixed hour are also the people who do everything else right — the lower blood fats may be theirs, not the hour's. (3) restates the doubt without grounding it; (2) and (4) do not bear on the comparison.

steps.stem: The minister for the environment claims that the Fruchter Industries factory caused even more pollution this year than last year. As evidence she notes that this year there were significantly more reports by factory workers of pollution resulting from the factory's operations than there were last year. Which of the following pieces of information shows that the evidence the minister cites cannot, on its own, establish her claim?
choices: Last year the factory's managers carried out a surprise inspection to identify sources of pollution in the factory
During a visit to the factory this year, a representative of the ministry gave the workers a lecture on the importance of reporting pollution
Many of the workers who reported pollution this year had themselves taken part in the operations that caused it
Last year the factory's management invested heavily in preventing pollution
explanation: More reports may reflect more reporting rather than more pollution. (4) supports the minister; (1) and (3) do not bear on the count of reports.

steps.stem: Dr. Segal: "Bees estimate the distance they have flown by the effort the flight required." Dr. Avrahami: "Bees estimate the distance they have flown by the number of objects they saw during the flight." Which of the following findings weakens Dr. Segal's claim without strengthening Dr. Avrahami's?
choices: Bees find it hard to estimate distances greater than five kilometers
Blind bees estimate distances less accurately than sighted bees
Bees find it hard to estimate distances in fog
Bees flying against a strong wind and bees flying in still air estimate the distance flown with equal accuracy
explanation: Equal accuracy despite unequal effort tells against effort, and says nothing about seeing. (2) and (3) strengthen Avrahami; (1) touches neither.

steps.stem: Dr. Malkov noticed that a large share of the patients who come to her clinic with the disease "hargashet" work at a computer for long hours. She concluded that prolonged work at a computer encourages the outbreak of the disease. Which of the following data would strengthen Dr. Malkov's conclusion?
choices: Computers emit a radiation known as "epsilon," which is suspected of causing the disease
Dr. Malkov's clinic is in an area in which many software companies are located
A study found that the disease tends to run in families
Prolonged sitting at a computer causes fatigue, and the disease too causes fatigue
explanation: A mechanism links the cause to the effect. (2) explains the observation without the cause; (3) offers a different cause; (4) confuses a shared symptom with a link.

steps.stem: The pupils of class 8A studied French with the teacher Efraim, and the pupils of class 8B with the teacher Yair. In the national examination in French, the average mark of 8A was higher than that of 8B. The principal supposed that Efraim's methods are more effective than Yair's; the deputy principal supposed instead that the pupils of 8A are more diligent than those of 8B. Which of the following data would weaken BOTH suppositions?
choices: The average mark of class 8C, which also studied with Yair, was lower than 8A's and higher than 8B's
In the national examination in history the average mark of 8B was higher than 8A's, though both classes studied history with the same teacher
Many of the pupils of 8A come from French-speaking homes, whereas none of the pupils of 8B does
A month before the examination Efraim fell ill and Yair taught both classes
explanation: A third cause of the gap that is neither the teacher nor the pupils' diligence. (2) tells against diligence only; (1) and (4) bear on the teacher only.

steps.stem: "The Bears' House," the second children's book of the writer Alexander Skot, sold few copies compared with his first, "Sea Dogs." The publisher judged that it sold less because it was marketed at a higher price than "Sea Dogs." Which of the following facts does NOT weaken the publisher's judgment?
choices: Skot's third book, "The Golden Fish," was marketed at a price lower than both earlier books, and sold more copies than either
"Sea Dogs" was printed in large type with colored illustrations, whereas "The Bears' House" was printed in small type without illustrations
In "The Bears' House" the hero is a villain, whereas in "Sea Dogs" the hero is a positive figure children readily identify with
Unlike "The Bears' House," "Sea Dogs" appeared at the start of the summer holidays, when many parents look for books for their children
explanation: A cheaper book selling more is what the price explanation predicts. (2), (3) and (4) each supply a different cause of the difference.

steps.stem: A study conducted in Denmark found that over the past twenty years the incidence of "tzeredet," a disease that causes temporary hoarseness, was higher in the city of Odense than in the country's other cities. The researchers supposed that the reason is the high level of air pollution in Odense. Which of the following facts does NOT weaken the researchers' supposition?
choices: The climate of Odense is especially cold and stormy, and cold raises the risk of contracting the disease
Until the "Odense Works" was founded two years ago, air pollution in the city was low
The disease mainly affects the elderly, and the share of the elderly in Odense's population is lower than the national average
Air pollution in Copenhagen is higher than in Odense, but the incidence of the disease there is very low
explanation: Fewer elderly makes the high incidence harder to explain, but offers no rival cause; (1) offers one, (2) breaks the timing, (4) breaks the correlation.

steps.stem: Recently a plan was proposed to pave a new fast road between two cities, on which the permitted speed will be higher than on the country's other roads, and which will therefore shorten the journey between the cities. Opponents of the plan argue that the road, if paved, will increase air pollution, because of the pollutants that cars emit. Which of the following facts does NOT support the opponents' claim?
choices: The shorter the journeys between cities, the more people tend to make such journeys
The longer a journey lasts, the more air pollution it causes
The more roads there are, the more cars there are
Driving at high speed causes more air pollution than driving the same distance at low speed
explanation: A road that shortens journeys would, by (2), reduce pollution — the opposite of the opponents' claim. (1), (3) and (4) each supply a route from the road to more pollution.

steps.stem: In a survey, people from different countries were asked to rate their happiness on a scale from one to ten, and it was found that the average happiness of the Americans was higher than that of the Indians. Professor Ilam argues that one cannot conclude from the survey that there is a gap in happiness between Americans and Indians. Which of the following is best suited to be the basis of her argument?
choices: In the United States the economy is more stable than in India, and the better a person's economic situation, the happier he is
The share of respondents who marked "7" among the American respondents equaled the share among the Indian respondents
Owing to an error, the results of several hundred American questionnaires were not included, and the average happiness among those respondents was found to be higher than among the other Americans
In Indian culture it is customary, even when one is very happy, to say that one is merely "content"
explanation: If the scale is answered differently in the two cultures, the numbers do not measure the same thing. (1) supports the gap; (3) would widen it; (2) is beside the point.

steps.stem: Menachem, the manager of the "Muscles" gym, noticed that only a few of the gym's members are over forty. He assumed that the reason is that among people over forty awareness of the importance of physical activity is lower than among the young. Shlomo, his assistant, pointed to a datum that led Menachem to change his mind. Which of the following is most likely to be the datum Shlomo pointed to?
choices: The training equipment at "Muscles" is old, and the gym offers only a small range of activities
The rival gym "Samson" began to offer a reduced price to people over forty, but this did not increase their number among its members
Next door to "Muscles" operates the successful gym "Weights," the only gym in the city that offers classes designed especially for people over forty
Among the members of "Muscles," the share of those aged twenty to thirty is higher than the share of those aged thirty to forty
explanation: The over-forties are exercising — elsewhere. (2) supports Menachem's assumption; (1) and (4) do not bear on the age group's awareness.

steps.stem: Oded drank a glass of wine at a party and afterwards felt dizzy. An hour later he drank the beverage "El Abismo," and felt the dizziness pass. From this Oded concluded that licorice, a substance found in "El Abismo," neutralizes the effect of alcohol. Which of the following data does NOT weaken Oded's conclusion?
choices: "El Abismo" contains a good deal of sugar, and sugar is known to help dispel dizziness
Studies show that the effect of the alcohol in a glass of wine on a man of Oded's weight passes after half an hour
The wine Oded drank contained a negligible amount of alcohol, but was made from a variety of grape to which Oded is allergic, and his allergy shows itself in dizziness
Oded drinks a cup of a licorice-rich beverage almost every day, and drinking it has never made him dizzy
explanation: That licorice does not cause dizziness says nothing about whether it relieves the dizziness of alcohol. (1) supplies another active ingredient, (2) the passage of time, (3) another cause of the dizziness.

steps.stem: In a study of the properties of the papaya root it was found that the root improves mood. The researchers supposed that alpha, one of the substances in the root, is responsible for the effect. A similar effect, however, was not found in participants who swallowed tablets containing alpha, and the researchers therefore concluded that their supposition had been mistaken. Which of the following findings would strengthen the researchers' conclusion?
choices: The mood of participants who ate papaya roots that contain no alpha did not improve
Participants who ate papaya roots were, on average, sadder than participants who did not
There was no difference in the improvement of mood between participants who ate papaya roots and participants who ate roots from which the alpha had been extracted
The tablets the participants swallowed contained another substance, beta, which neutralizes alpha
explanation: If the root works as well without alpha, alpha is not the cause. (1) supports the supposition; (4) rescues it by explaining the tablets' failure; (2) is beside the point.

steps.stem: Maya watched the television news every day for a week and noticed that no football matches were mentioned in the news. She concluded that no football matches had been played that week. Which of the following facts would weaken Maya's conclusion?
choices: The television news makes a point of covering events in every field of life
In that week there were no events that could have overshadowed football matches
The television channels report football matches only in their sports programs
The weather that week was fine, and matches could have been played
explanation: If the news never carries football, its silence proves nothing. (1) and (2) strengthen the inference; (4) shows matches were possible, not that they happened.

steps.stem: Until the beginning of the twentieth century the Japanese ate almost no meat, and diagnoses of the disease "gamelet" among them were few. Today, as Western eating habits have penetrated Japan, a marked rise is recorded in the number of cases of gamelet in Japanese hospitals. From this researchers concluded that eating meat raises the risk of gamelet. Which of the following facts would weaken the researchers' conclusion?
choices: Life expectancy in Japan is still among the highest in the world
Compared with the beginning of the twentieth century, there has been a real fall in the number of Japanese suffering from anemia, and meat is known to be rich in iron
The diagnostic methods in Japanese hospitals have improved greatly over the past hundred years
Among Japanese families who emigrated to the West and adopted Western eating habits, the incidence of gamelet resembles that in the general Western population
explanation: More diagnoses may mean better diagnosis, not more disease. (4) supports the conclusion; (1) and (2) do not bear on it.

steps.stem: Tali wished to choose for her mobile telephone the ringtone her parents would like best out of the ten available. To that end she played the ten ringtones to her parents and asked them to grade each of them, giving the highest grade to the ringtone most pleasant to their ear. When she added up the results, Tali found that the ringtone that received the highest grade was the one with the highest pitch. Which of the following facts casts doubt on the reliability of Tali's test?
choices: Tali's father is hoarse
Tali's mother says that birdsong, which was not among the ten ringtones, is her favorite sound
Tali's mother said that she had an earache and found it hard to listen to the last ringtones
Tali's father calls Tali's mobile telephone only rarely
explanation: If the last ringtones were not heard properly, the grades do not compare like with like. (1), (2) and (4) do not affect the grading.

steps.stem: A teacher noticed that the pupils who attended the revision lesson he gave before the examination did not succeed in it more than the pupils who did not attend. He concluded that the revision lesson did not help. Which of the following data could cause the teacher to retract his conclusion?
choices: Only pupils who were away on a school trip were absent from the revision lesson
The pupils who attended the revision lesson are the more diligent and motivated pupils
The pupils who already commanded the material well preferred to study at home on their own
Pupils who attended a revision lesson given by another teacher for the same examination scored lower on average than pupils who did not
explanation: If the strong pupils stayed away, equal results mean the lesson lifted the weaker ones. (2) makes the null result worse for the lesson; (1) and (4) do not bear on it.

steps.stem: A pharmaceutical company wished to test the effectiveness of a new pill for losing weight. It compared a trial group with a control group; both groups followed the same diet, but the trial group also took the pill. After a month the trial group weighed less, on average, than the control group, and the company concluded that the pill improves the diet's effectiveness. Which of the following data does NOT weaken the company's conclusion?
choices: The developers of the pill do not know what mechanism underlies its action
Besides taking the pill, the members of the trial group were encouraged to exercise
Before the trial the members of the trial group weighed more, on average, than the members of the control group, and heavier people lose weight faster
Some members of the trial group who saw that their weight was not falling dropped out, and their data were deleted
explanation: Not knowing how a thing works does not show that it does not work. (2) is a confound, (3) a difference at baseline, (4) a biased sample.

steps.stem: The sales of down coats of the company "Beni and Sons" rose by thirty percent last month. Beni estimated that the rise stemmed from the cold wave that struck the country in that period. Which of the following data would weaken Beni's estimate?
choices: The sales of the company's down quilts also rose last month
At the same time as the cold wave, Beni launched an advertising campaign for the company's products
In the preceding period the company's sales fell by twenty percent
In that period the rival company "Batya and Daughters" lowered the prices of its coats
explanation: A rival cause that coincides with the cold. (1) supports the cold explanation; (3) and (4) do not bear on it.

steps.stem: The lecturer in the course "Introduction to Hebrew Literature" noticed that all the students of the biology department who take his course regularly arrive late to lessons. He concluded that students who take courses outside their own department do not bother to arrive on time. Which of the following data would strengthen the lecturer's conclusion?
choices: The building in which the course is taught is far from the biology department's building
The literature students who attend the lessons in "Applied Biology" regularly arrive late
The biology students arrive late to all their lessons, including those in biology
The literature students also arrive late to "Introduction to Hebrew Literature"
explanation: The same pattern in the opposite direction. (1) supplies another cause; (3) and (4) show lateness unrelated to the department.

steps.stem: A report on road accidents in the town of Ein-Moshe in the years 1995–2000 shows that the number of pedestrians hurt while crossing at a green light was greater than the number hurt while crossing at a red light. Following the report the head of the council decided to remove the pedestrian traffic lights, claiming that they do not reduce the risk. Which of the following data explains why the council head's claim is mistaken?
choices: The number of pedestrians in Ein-Moshe is small compared with the number of cars
In Tel-Pinchas, a neighboring town, the number of pedestrians hurt at a red light was greater than the number hurt at a green light
Pedestrians crossing at a green light look to the sides less than pedestrians crossing at a red light
The number of pedestrians who cross at a green light is many times the number who cross at a red light
explanation: More injuries at green because far more crossings at green; the rate per crossing may be far lower. (3) explains the count without touching the rate; (1) and (2) are beside the point.

steps.stem: On checking the data after the results had been published, it turned out that Dr. Ashi had interchanged the average life spans of group A and group C.
choices: Strengthens A, weakens B
Weakens A, strengthens B
Strengthens both
Weakens both
explanation: With alpha at three years and no supplement at five, alpha is worse than beta and both supplements are worse than none.

steps.stem: In the room in which the mice of group B lived, the temperature throughout the experiment was much higher than the temperature best suited to mice.
choices: Strengthens A, weakens B
Weakens A, strengthens B
Strengthens both
Weakens both
explanation: Beta's true effect was masked by the heat, so alpha's advantage over it is in doubt — and beta beat no-supplement despite the handicap, which strengthens the case for supplements.

steps.stem: Earlier studies found that the more mice are exposed to noise in their surroundings, the shorter their lives. Group B was exposed to far more noise than group C, but to slightly less than group A.
choices: Strengthens A, weakens B
Weakens A, strengthens B
Strengthens both
Weakens both
explanation: Group A outlived group B despite more noise, so alpha's edge over beta is real; group B outlived group C despite far more noise, so a supplement helps.

steps.stem: In a study of infant car seats, parents were asked to seat their infants in two ways: for one hour facing the parents, and for one hour facing the direction of travel. The researchers found that when the infants faced their parents they tended to smile more, and concluded that when infants see their parents' faces they feel better. Which of the following facts does NOT weaken the researchers' conclusion?
choices: In the second half of the trial all the infants faced the direction of travel, and many of them fell asleep
Some of the parents who took part in the study were experienced parents, and for some the infant was their first child
When the infants faced the direction of travel they were more exposed to the wind blowing through the window
The seats in which the infants faced their parents were more comfortable than those in which they faced the direction of travel
explanation: The parents' experience does not bear on why the infants smiled. (1), (3) and (4) each offer a reason other than the parents' faces.

steps.stem: Shula lived longer than Leah. Shula's daughter attributes the difference to hereditary factors. Leah's daughter argues that the difference stems from the fact that Shula lived in a mountainous region with clear air, whereas Leah lived in a city with heavy air pollution. Which of the following facts would weaken BOTH claims?
choices: Shula and Leah were sisters
Shula was stricter about healthy nutrition than Leah
Shula and Leah were equally strict about healthy nutrition
The region in which Shula lived has clear air, but the air there is thin
explanation: A third cause. (1) tells against heredity alone; (3) removes a rival rather than adding one; (4) touches the air claim alone.

steps.stem: Most of the carpentry workshops in the city of Petzro are concentrated in "Carpenters' Street." Osnat, who has just completed her training as a carpenter, was advised NOT to open her new workshop in that street. Which of the following facts could be a consideration against the advice?
choices: People looking for furniture in Carpenters' Street start at its southern end, and sometimes tire before they reach the northern end, and the reverse
The veteran carpenters in the street sometimes copy ideas from the newcomers
The Petzro municipality is about to approve a regulation granting tax relief to craft workshops in Carpenters' Street
Most suppliers of raw materials for carpentry are far from Carpenters' Street, and delays in supply occur
explanation: A benefit available only there. (2) and (4) support the advice; (1) is neutral or supports it.

steps.stem: Until the 1980s, the medical community believed that the level of acidity in the stomach was too high to enable bacteria to be found in it, and therefore bacteria could not possibly cause stomach ulcers. A scientific experiment disproved this assumption. Which of the following cannot be this experiment?
choices: Taking a sample of stomach cells from people with a stomach ulcer, and checking for the presence of bacteria in the sample
Creating an artificial environment with a level of acidity similar to that found in the stomach, and checking whether any bacteria survive in that environment
Treating a stomach ulcer with medication whose only effect is to kill bacteria, and checking whether the ulcer is cured by this treatment
Using antacids to reduce the level of acidity in the stomach, and checking whether there are bacteria in the stomach after the level of acidity has been reduced

steps.stem: Udi noticed that whenever Iris has math homework due for Thursday's class, she only does it on Wednesday evening. He assumed that Iris puts off doing her homework until the last minute because she prefers to do her study assignments when she is pressed for time. Which of the following statements does not weaken Udi's assumption?
choices: Iris has a biology class on Friday morning, and she does her homework for it on Sunday evening
Iris's math class is at 7:30 on Thursday morning, and therefore she has to get up earlier on Thursdays than on any other day of the week
Iris's older sister gives private math lessons, and she comes to visit Iris every Wednesday evening
Iris has after-school activities every evening except for Wednesday

steps.stem: A study found that Mexican people suffer from headaches more than English people do. Based on the fact that Mexican people eat mainly tropical fruits, whereas English people eat mainly other fruits, the researchers hypothesized that excess intake of pectin, a substance found in fruits, causes headaches. Which of the following assumptions did the researchers rely on for their hypothesis?
choices: Compared to England, in Mexico people eat a lot of pectin-rich foods that are not tropical fruits
Low intake levels of pectin help prevent headaches
There is less pectin in the fruits that English people eat than in tropical fruits
The main cause of headaches is eating pectin-rich fruits

steps.stem: Professor Shore: "Were it not for the recent publication of old photographs of the Urdu tribe members that were not taken by anthropologists, I would have found it difficult to support those who agree with Professor Jamil's claim about the sources of photographs of the tribe members." Which of the following is not implied by Professor Shore?
choices: Professors Jamil and Shore now hold a similar opinion about the photographs of the Urdu tribe members
Photographs of the Urdu tribe members taken by anthropologists were published recently
Until recently, Professor Shore believed that the only photographs of the Urdu tribe members were taken by anthropologists
Professor Jamil claimed that it was not only anthropologists who took photographs of the Urdu tribe members

steps.stem: Researchers wished to examine which form of medication is more effective in reducing fever in children: syrup or tablets. They divided one hundred sick children, who had come to the clinic with fever, into two groups: fifty children aged 4-7 were given the medication as a syrup, and fifty children aged 8-11 were given the medication as a tablet. After the medication began to take effect, the researchers measured the children's temperature, and found that the average temperature of the children who took the medication as a tablet was lower than that of the children who took it as a syrup. Based on this, the researchers concluded that the medication is more effective in tablet form. Which of the following weakens the researchers' conclusion?
choices: The younger the children, the higher their temperature tends to be when they are sick
Older children tend to become sick less often than younger children
In each group, there were several children who did not manage to take the medication
The children in both groups became sick for a variety of reasons
